query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Classifies incidents (software/hardware/etc). This partly defines/identifies the outcome (which incidents are hardware) rather than acting as a treatment or common cause; it is closer to outcome stratification than a confounder.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The specific failure manifestation (connectivity_failure, overheating, not_powering_on) lies on the causal path between an underlying cause and the recorded incident; it describes how the incident occurred rather than a common cause of a treatment and the spike.

per_column.name: software_update_triggered
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause (a software update event) whose effect on the hardware-incident spike could be attributed. It is a plausible intervention/exposure surfaced from the data.

per_column.name: incident_action_type
per_column.rationale: The remediation action (repair/replacement/install) occurs downstream of the incident; it is a consequence/response, on the post-outcome path, not a common cause.

per_column.name: recurring_caller
per_column.rationale: Specific callers/users could drive both exposure to updates/configurations (treatment) and the volume of incidents (outcome), acting as a plausible common cause that must be adjusted for. Surfaced from data, not the query.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Flags whether an incident is a recurrence; recurrence is a property determined by the incident/outcome itself and by prior causes, so conditioning on it risks collider bias rather than confounding control.

judge.rationale: A candidate treatment (software_update_triggered) is present, so a cause is offered. However genuine confounders -- common causes of BOTH the treatment and the hardware-incident spike -- are essentially absent. failure_mode and incident_action_type are mediators/downstream, incident_category is outcome stratification, and recurrence_signal is a collider. Only recurring_caller weakly qualifies as a common cause, and even that is tenuous. The column set does not credibly set up an unbiased causal estimation: it lacks temporal/load, environment, patch-schedule, or asset-age confounders that jointly drive updates and failures. Weak realisation of the causal-attribution claim.
